deploy.$comment: boot.py seeds the stores and then execs the API — it is not a wrapper that can be skipped. A startCommand of `python -m core.api.app` boots an API over an empty volume, because Kuzu is single-writer and the API holds the lock.
deploy.$timeout_comment: The FIRST boot after a data epoch does real work before the API binds, and it CANNOT be deferred: Kuzu is single-writer and the API holds the lock for as long as it serves, so there is no moment after startup when the graph can be filled. A COLD VOLUME must load all three GDELT artifacts (china 66,669 + eurasia 95,070 + mena 104,860 = ~267k merges) plus the deep tier, the study backlog and the forecast freeze. Measured on Railway at roughly 110 events/sec, that is ~40min of GDELT alone, so the window is 5400s. This is a ONE-TIME cost per volume: every later boot finds the counts already satisfied and skips in milliseconds. A window too SHORT is the expensive failure — it kills a container that was working, which is what happened on 2026-08-12.
